product: Nimbus Buds Lite (budget true wireless earbuds)

reviews.text: Great sound for the price. Bass is punchy and the case fits in my coin pocket.
Left bud keeps disconnecting from the right one every few minutes. Returned them.
Battery gets me through a full workday, about 6 hours, and the case adds two more charges.
They hurt my ears after an hour. The smallest tips are still too big for me.
Box arrived crushed but the earbuds inside were fine. Sound is decent, nothing special.
Wow, a whole 90 minutes of battery. Truly a marvel of modern engineering.
Does anyone know if these work with a PS5? Haven't opened them yet.
For $25 I expected garbage. They're not garbage. Sound is clear, they stay in during the gym, and pairing took five seconds.
One earbud stopped charging after three weeks.
Me encantan. Suenan muy bien y la batería dura todo el día. El envío tardó casi tres semanas, eso sí.
Loud enough for a backyard party and the bass doesn't distort at max volume.
Fell off a picnic table onto concrete, not a scratch, still works perfectly.
Arrived with a cracked grille, packed in a flimsy envelope with no padding.
The connection drops if I walk into the next room, even with the door open. Range is maybe 5 meters.
Battery is fine. Sound is fine. Price is fine. It's a speaker.
Sounds fuller than my old JBL Flip 4 and costs less.
Twelve hours of playback at half volume, exactly as advertised. Charges over USB-C in about two hours.
Stopped turning on after two months. Support wanted me to pay shipping both ways for the warranty repair.
The app is useless and keeps asking me to create an account. The speaker itself sounds great.
Overpriced for what it is. You can get the same sound for half the money.
Noise cancelling is unreal. I can't hear the plane engine at all.
Clamp force is brutal. Headache after 40 minutes every single time.
Battery lasts forever. I charge them maybe once every ten days.
Mic is terrible on calls, everyone says I sound like I'm in a tunnel. Music sounds great though.
Headband cracked at the hinge after four months of normal use.
At $349 these should come with a better case. Sound and ANC are excellent, but the price stings.
Multipoint works perfectly between my laptop and phone. Switching is seamless.
Delivered a day early, well packaged.

I bought these for my daily train commute after two years with the Sony XM5, so this is mostly a comparison. Sound is warmer than the Sony and I prefer it for jazz and acoustic stuff; vocals are especially nice. They are also noticeably lighter, and the ear cups don't get hot the way the Sony ones did on long trips. Battery is excellent, I get roughly 30 hours and only charge them on Sundays. The weak point is the connection: if my phone is in my back pocket the audio cuts out for a second every few minutes, which never happened with the Sony. And they cost $349 while the XM5 is often on sale for $280, which is hard to justify. Would I buy them again? Probably, but I would wait for a discount.
Oh great, another pair of 'premium' headphones whose ear pads started peeling in a month. Love that for me.
They're comfortable enough for a long flight, and the sound is good.
Can these be used with a wired cable on a plane?
Bluetooth keeps cutting out when I'm at the gym.
Valen cada peso. Las uso todo el día en la oficina y no me molestan para nada.
Ear cups get really hot in summer and my ears sweat after half an hour.
The sound is so flat and lifeless I checked twice that I hadn't left a podcast EQ on. Returning.
Battery lasts forever, I charge them maybe once every ten days!
Package said delivered but it showed up at my neighbor's three days later.
Everything about these is great except the battery, which lasts about half as long as my old Bose.
Good value. Paid $199 on sale and they compete with headphones twice the price.

product: Stride Sport (wireless sport earbuds with ear hooks)

reviews.text: Never fall out, even on 10-mile runs.
Sweat killed the right earbud in five weeks. So much for 'IPX5'.
Battery: 7 hours. Sound: punchy. Fit: secure. Exactly what I wanted.
The ear hooks dig into the back of my ears after an hour.
Audio skips every time my phone is in my left pocket.
Sound is thin and tinny, but I mostly listen to podcasts, so I don't care. Price was right.
Arrived in two days. Haven't tried them yet.
Love them!!!
Third pair in a year. They keep breaking at the charging contacts. I keep buying them because nothing else stays in my ears.
Lol 'all-day battery'. Mine die before my lunch run is over.
The case lid snapped off within a month.
Took me 20 minutes and a factory reset to get them to pair with my iPhone.
Cheap, light, and they survive the rain. Can't ask for more at this price.
Me duran cinco horas corriendo y no se caen nunca. Muy recomendados.
Bass is weak compared to my AirPods Pro, but the fit is far better for running.
Box was open and one ear tip was missing when it arrived.
Is the charging case wireless or USB-C only?
Never fall out, even on 10 mile runs!
Mic picks up a lot of wind noise on runs. Calls are basically impossible outside.
Paid $59, worth it for the battery alone.
Positional audio is incredible. I can hear exactly where footsteps are coming from.
Wireless dongle has zero lag. Feels like a wired headset.
Battery lasts about 20 hours with RGB off, which covers a whole weekend of gaming.
Heavy. My neck hurts after a long session.
The left ear cup stopped working after two months.
Mic quality is great, my squad says I sound crystal clear.
Way too expensive for what you get.
Arrived a week late with no tracking updates.
Super comfy memory foam pads, I forget I'm wearing them.
Sounds muddy when I listen to music. Bass drowns out everything.
Dongle disconnects randomly mid-match. Lost a ranked game because of it.
Wow, the headband snapped on day three. Built like a tank, clearly.
Bought it on Black Friday for $99. Steal.
Battery barely lasts one evening of gaming. I have to charge it every day.
Great headset overall, but the ear cups get warm after an hour.
Can I use this with an Xbox?
Software is bloated and crashes constantly.
The surround sound actually helps me in Valorant, and it's light enough for 6-hour sessions.
Came in perfect condition, double boxed.
After a year of daily use, still works like new.

Coming from a wired HyperX Cloud II, which I used for four years. The soundstage on the Kestrel is clearly wider, and in shooters I can place enemies much more precisely than before. The 2.4 GHz dongle has no noticeable lag, and the signal holds even when I walk to the kitchen for a drink. Battery has been great too: I play three or four hours most evenings and charge it once a week. My problem is comfort. I wear glasses, and the clamp presses the arms into my head, so after two hours I have to take it off. The Cloud II never did that. Also, $180 is a lot when the Cloud II cost me $90, and the jump in quality does not feel like double. Good headset, but not the upgrade I hoped for at this price.
Pairing with my phone over Bluetooth while using the dongle works great, I can take calls while gaming.
The volume wheel broke off within a month.
Positional audio is incredible, I can hear exactly where the footsteps come from!
Muy cómodos y el sonido es espectacular, pero la batería no dura nada.
Box was soaked and torn when it arrived. Delivery driver left it in the rain.
My kid uses it for Fortnite and hasn't complained once, which is a first.
Sound is decent, but for $180 I expected way more.
Charges fully in about two hours over USB-C and lasts days.
Constant static hiss in the background, even with nothing playing.
Ear pads are already flaking after 3 months.
Fits fine with my glasses, no pressure at all.
Better than my Arctis 7 in every way except price.
Range is amazing. I can walk to the kitchen and still hear my team.
Return window closed one day before it died. Great timing.
Shipping was fast and the sound is good. No complaints.
Mic monitoring is a nice touch.
Way too tight on my head, and I don't have a big head.
Worth the price for the wireless performance alone.
Battery indicator is wrong, says 50% then dies ten minutes later.

Overpriced. The $15 ones from the supermarket do the same thing.
Survived being thrown down the stairs by a toddler, twice!

We bought two pairs for an eight-hour road trip with our kids, ages 7 and 9. Both pairs lasted the entire drive on one charge, which honestly surprised me. The sound is clear for cartoons and audiobooks, and I like that the volume cap means I don't have to worry about their ears. Unfortunately, by the end of the trip the hinge on one pair had cracked, and my kids are not rough with their things. On the plus side, they arrived the day after I ordered them. At this price I would buy them again, even if I have to replace a pair now and then.
My kids fight over who gets to use them.
Hinge cracked after a month of gentle use.

Shipped quickly and well packed.

Wow, battery lasted a full 40 minutes. My kid was thrilled. Not.
